title: Resolve known task paths to make one context brief sufficient
context: Lexical lookup of a symptom combined with a filename could return only symbols, omitting file-scoped invariants and prior decisions. Existing instructions also required redundant memory queries. Touches invariant(s): con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Resolve explicit known repository paths embedded in task phrases and merge their scoped memory by record ID. Treat one adequate context brief as sufficient, with follow-up queries only for missing information, uncovered scope, risk, or new evidence that changes the target.
consequences: Embedded relative paths, absolute repository paths, line references, and Markdown links retain scoped memory and blast radius.
Visibility filtering remains authoritative; outside and unknown paths do not borrow another file's memory.
Routine implementation of existing decisions skips duplicate capture.
alternatives_rejected: Rely on lexical lookup alone for task phrases containing known file paths.
Require another context call before every edit or treat follow-up tools as a per-task checklist.
